original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › JOHN GALT: Invented the motor — static electricity engine that could power the world
final_text: Dagny and Rearden find the wreck of Galt's motor, which drew static electricity from the atmosphere, in the abandoned Twentieth Century Motor Company factory at Starnesville, Wisconsin.
source_note: Plot: motor found in abandoned factory

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › JOHN GALT: Walked away when his company nationalized his invention
final_text: Galt quit the Twentieth Century Motor Company when the Starnes heirs imposed pay by need instead of ability; he was the first man to walk out, not a victim of nationalization.
source_note: Jeff Allen's account, Part Two Ch. 10

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › JOHN GALT: Works as track laborer at Taggart Transcontinental — hiding in plain sight
final_text: For twelve years Galt worked as a track laborer in the underground tunnels of the Taggart Terminal in New York, beneath Dagny's own railroad.
source_note: Galt hidden as Taggart laborer

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › JOHN GALT: The man who stopped the motor of the world
final_text: The tramp Jeff Allen, taken into Dagny's car on the Comet, tells how Galt swore he would stop the motor of the world (Part Two, 'The Sign of the Dollar').
source_note: Part Two Chapter 10 summary

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › JOHN GALT: "I am the man who loves his life"
final_text: "I am the man who loves his life"
source_note: Line from opening of Galt's radio speech

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › HANK REARDEN: Self-made industrialist, invented Rearden Metal
final_text: Rearden Metal, a greenish-blue alloy of iron and copper, cost Hank Rearden ten years of experiments; the novel shows its first heat poured at his mills.
source_note: Rearden Metal development, Part One

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › HANK REARDEN: Married to a wife who hates him (Lillian) — guilt as weapon
final_text: Lillian Rearden betrays Hank's affair with Dagny to James Taggart; Dr. Floyd Ferris uses it to blackmail Rearden into signing Rearden Metal over through the 'Gift Certificate'.
source_note: Government blackmail over the affair

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › HANK REARDEN: His journey: from accepting unearned guilt to rejecting it
final_text: Tried for an illegal sale of Rearden Metal to Ken Danagger, Rearden refuses to recognize the court's right to try him; the cowed judges hand down a suspended sentence.
source_note: Part Two Ch. 4, 'The Sanction of the Victim'

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › HANK REARDEN: "I work for nothing but my own profit — which I make by selling a product they need to men who are willing and able to buy it"
final_text: "I work for nothing but my own profit — which I make by selling a product they need to men who are willing and able to buy it"
source_note: Rearden's speech at his trial

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › HANK REARDEN: The bracelet of Rearden Metal — first thing he forged, given to Lillian (who despises it), later worn by Dagny (who understands it)
final_text: The bracelet made from the first pour of Rearden Metal is his anniversary gift to Lillian, who mocks it; at the party Dagny trades her diamond bracelet for it (Part One, 'The Non-Commercial').
source_note: Anniversary party scene, Part One Ch. 6

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › FRANCISCO D'ANCONIA: Heir to the world's greatest copper fortune, fifth generation
final_text: Francisco is heir to the centuries-old d'Anconia Copper fortune, founded by Sebastián d'Anconia, who left Spain after defying the Inquisition and rebuilt in Argentina.
source_note: Centuries-old fortune; generation count unsourced

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › FRANCISCO D'ANCONIA: Dagny's first love, childhood friend
final_text: Francisco spent childhood summers with Dagny and Eddie at the Taggart estate on the Hudson, and later became Dagny's first lover.
source_note: Childhood friendship and first love

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › FRANCISCO D'ANCONIA: Brilliance masked as playboy — deliberately destroying his fortune
final_text: Francisco sinks investors' money into the worthless San Sebastián copper mines in Mexico, then lets the People's State of Mexico nationalize them: a deliberate trap for the looters.
source_note: Francisco hurting his company intentionally

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › FRANCISCO D'ANCONIA: The money speech at James's wedding: "Until you discover that money is the root of all good..."
final_text: At James Taggart's wedding reception Francisco says: "Until and unless you discover that money is the root of all good, you ask for your own destruction."
source_note: Verbatim text of the money speech

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › FRANCISCO D'ANCONIA: "If you saw Atlas shrugging — what would you tell him?" "To shrug."
final_text: Francisco puts the Atlas question to Hank Rearden at his mills (Part Two, Ch. 3): what would you tell the buckling giant to do? His answer: "To shrug."
source_note: Francisco to Rearden, Part Two Ch. 3

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › RAGNAR DANNESKJÖLD: Norwegian philosopher turned pirate
final_text: Ragnar Danneskjöld studied philosophy at Patrick Henry University under Hugh Akston, alongside Francisco and Galt, before becoming a pirate.
source_note: Akston student turned pirate

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › RAGNAR DANNESKJÖLD: Seizes welfare-state ships, converts to gold, returns to producers
final_text: Ragnar raids government relief ships and returns the value in gold to producers as refunds of their income taxes; he hands Rearden a bar of gold, 'a small refund on a very large debt'.
source_note: Part Two Ch. 7, 'The Moratorium on Brains'

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › RAGNAR DANNESKJÖLD: "I am the first man to make piracy a moral profession"
final_text: Ragnar tells Rearden he is out to destroy Robin Hood: he is "the man who robs the thieving poor and gives back to the productive rich."
source_note: Ragnar on Robin Hood, Part Two Ch. 7

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › RAGNAR DANNESKJÖLD: The Viking who fights for the mind
final_text: In Galt's Gulch Ragnar's wife is Kay Ludlow, the Hollywood actress who joined the strike.
source_note: Kay Ludlow joins strike, marries Ragnar

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › EDDIE WILLERS: Dagny's assistant, everyman, deeply loyal
final_text: The novel opens on Eddie Willers remembering the great oak on the Taggart estate he thought eternal, until lightning showed it was hollow inside.
source_note: Part One Ch. 1 opening image

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › EDDIE WILLERS: Talks to the nameless track worker (Galt) in the cafeteria
final_text: Talks to the nameless track worker (Galt) in the cafeteria
source_note: Eddie confides in unnamed worker

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › EDDIE WILLERS: Cannot follow to the Gulch — left on a stalled train in the desert
final_text: In the last chapter Eddie Willers is left alone beside the stalled Taggart Comet in the desert, trying to restart its dead engine.
source_note: Part Three Ch. 10 ending

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › EDDIE WILLERS: The most tragic figure: a good man who needs the creators but isn't one
final_text: "Who is John Galt?" are the novel's first words, asked of Eddie Willers by a bum on a New York street at dusk.
source_note: Opening line, Part One Ch. 1

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › OBJECTIVISM (as expressed in Atlas Shrugged): Reality exists independent of consciousness (A is A)
final_text: Galt's speech: "A leaf cannot be a stone at the same time... A is A." Part Three of the novel is titled "A Is A".
source_note: Galt's Speech, law of identity

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › OBJECTIVISM (as expressed in Atlas Shrugged): Reason is man's only absolute
final_text: Galt's speech: "Existence is Identity, Consciousness is Identification."
source_note: Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual 125

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › OBJECTIVISM (as expressed in Atlas Shrugged): Self-interest is moral — sacrifice is not virtue
final_text: Galt's speech: "The creed of sacrifice is a morality for the immoral."
source_note: Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual 139

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › OBJECTIVISM (as expressed in Atlas Shrugged): No one has the right to another's mind, labor, or life
final_text: Galt's speech: "no man may initiate—do you hear me? no man may start—the use of physical force against others."
source_note: Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual 133

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › OBJECTIVISM (as expressed in Atlas Shrugged): The sanction of the victim: never help your destroyers
final_text: The sanction of the victim means producers withdrawing moral consent from their exploiters; Part Two, Ch. 4, where Rearden defies his court, bears that title.
source_note: Chapter title and strike principle

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › OBJECTIVISM (as expressed in Atlas Shrugged): Capitalism as the only moral economic system
final_text: Francisco: "If you ask me to name the proudest distinction of Americans, I would choose the fact that they were the people who created the phrase 'to make money.'"
source_note: Verbatim, money speech

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › OBJECTIVISM (as expressed in Atlas Shrugged): "Man's ego is the fountainhead of human progress"
final_text: Galt's speech: "To live, man must hold three things as the supreme and ruling values of his life: Reason—Purpose—Self-esteem."
source_note: Ego line not in Atlas; Galt's Speech

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › KEY QUOTES: "Who is John Galt?" — the world's resignation, later its answer
final_text: "Who is John Galt?" was coined by Twentieth Century Motor workers after Galt walked out and the plant failed, as if he had stopped the motor of the world.
source_note: Jeff Allen's account of the phrase's origin

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › KEY QUOTES: "I swear by my life and my love of it that I will never live for the sake of another man, nor ask another man to live for mine"
final_text: "I swear by my life and my love of it that I will never live for the sake of another man, nor ask another man to live for mine"
source_note: Galt oath, Part Three Ch. 1

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › KEY QUOTES: "The question isn't who is going to let me; it's who is going to stop me"
final_text: Against public doubt Dagny names her rebuilt Rio Norte Line the John Galt Line; its first run on Rearden Metal rails is a triumph (Part One, Ch. 8).
source_note: Quote is a misattribution; John Galt Line

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › KEY QUOTES: "If you saw Atlas, the giant who holds the world on his shoulders... what would you tell him to do? To shrug."
final_text: Francisco: "If you saw Atlas, the giant who holds the world on his shoulders... what would you tell him to do?" Rearden: "I... don't know." Francisco: "To shrug."
source_note: Part Two Ch. 3, Francisco to Rearden

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › KEY QUOTES: "Money is the barometer of a society's virtue"
final_text: "Money is the barometer of a society's virtue"
source_note: Verbatim, money speech

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › KEY QUOTES: "There are two sides to every issue: one side is right and the other is wrong, but the middle is always evil"
final_text: "There are two sides to every issue: one side is right and the other is wrong, but the middle is always evil"
source_note: Galt's speech

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › KEY QUOTES: "The ladder of success is best climbed by stepping on the rungs of opportunity"
final_text: Francisco opens his money speech at the wedding reception with: "So you think that money is the root of all evil?"
source_note: Not Rand; real money-speech opening

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › KEY QUOTES: "Run for your life from any man who tells you that money is evil"
final_text: "Run for your life from any man who tells you that money is evil"
source_note: Verbatim; next: leper's bell of a looter

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › KEY QUOTES: "Wealth is the product of man's capacity to think"
final_text: "Wealth is the product of man's capacity to think"
source_note: Verbatim, money speech

original: ATLAS SHRUGGED - Ayn Rand's Opus (1957) › KEY QUOTES: "Do not let your fire go out... do not let the hero in your soul perish"
final_text: "Do not let your fire go out... do not let the hero in your soul perish"
source_note: Close of Galt's speech
